one_liner: Mid-level contracting officer track at NGA: plan purchases, solicit and evaluate bids, negotiate, award, modify and close out government contracts; requires TS/SCI with polygraph.
fit_summary: The posting has three mandatory criteria: hands-on contract negotiation and management across contract types, drafting or reviewing contract modifications, and interpreting regulations for compliance. We don't know whether Daniel's IEM role involved any of that. Daniel's policy knowledge and relationship skills match the 'collaborative customer service' desirable item, but IA-03 is a full-performance band. Without direct contracting or proposal and contract-management work at IEM, Daniel likely will not pass the mandatory screen.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens); no federal status needed, and it is DCIPS Excepted Service.
Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution is mandatory (DoD contracting standard exceptions apply); confirm Daniel's degree.
Must obtain and keep a Top Secret/SCI clearance, pass a counterintelligence polygraph and drug test, and file an annual SF-714 financial disclosure.
Resume must show specific examples meeting all three mandatory criteria: regulatory interpretation, managing multiple contract types, and contract modifications.
Must earn DAWIA Contracting certification within 36 months, then complete 40 continuous learning hours per year.
strategy: Before applying, list every contract-related task Daniel actually did at IEM. Examples: supporting proposals to government clients, tracking task orders, reviewing scope or modifications, or working FEMA/Stafford Act or 2 CFR 200 compliance. Apply only if you can honestly document all three mandatory criteria.

Frame IEM work from the contractor side of government acquisition. Proposal development, interpreting RFP terms and conditions, monitoring deliverables against the statement of work, and resolving performance issues with the client all count if they are true.
Build the resume in the NGA resume builder, kept to 2 pages. Show dates, hours per week, and one concrete example with its result for each mandatory criterion, using the posting's exact wording.
Add a short cover letter, since NGA recommends one. Use it to connect your policy and regulatory knowledge, stakeholder skills, and disaster-recovery contracting exposure to the desirable criteria.

Apply between October 19 and October 31, 2026, and start early because the posting window is short. Then prepare for a long clearance process; keep employment, address, and financial records ready for the SF-86.

If you lack contracting experience, consider entry-level contract specialist trainee programs (for example, DoD 1102 interns) or the IA-02 band, and look at FAC-C or DAU foundational coursework to strengthen future applications.
resume_bullets: Interpreted [FEMA Public Assistance / 2 CFR 200 / client contract terms] to identify compliance risks on [number] [disaster recovery] projects and recommended mitigations adopted by [client], [result].

Supported negotiation and management of [Fixed Price / Time and Material / Cost Reimbursable] contracts and task orders valued at [$ amount] for [government client], resolving [type of performance issue] by [action].
Drafted or reviewed [number] contract modifications for accuracy and completeness, coordinating scope, cost and schedule changes with [client/program office] to [outcome].
interview_questions: Describe a time you interpreted a regulation or contract clause to identify a risk. What did you recommend?
Walk us through the differences between fixed price, cost reimbursable, and T&M contracts and when each fits.
Tell us about a contractor performance problem you helped resolve and how you documented it.
How would you build a working relationship with a demanding internal customer who wants an award faster than the process allows?
watch_outs: The mandatory contracting experience may not match Daniel's IEM role; applicants who don't meet all three criteria are screened out.
Requires a bachelor's degree, TS/SCI, a polygraph, and an annual financial disclosure, and clearance processing can take many months.
The application window is short (October 19–31, 2026). The posting is telework-ineligible, and NGA may place you in any role or location after clearance.
